title: Horizontal Drain Transitions: Sanitary Tee vs. Wye
description: Choosing the correct fitting for horizontal drain transitions is critical to prevent flow obstruction and back-up issues. A standard sanitary tee is designed for transitioning flow from horizontal to vertical branches. Installing a sanitary tee flat on its side in a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage line creates turbulence and allows waste to flow backward or collect at the branch junction. Instead, always use a wye with a 1/8 bend or a combination wye and 1/8 bend for horizontal drainage direction changes to direct waste smoothly downstream in the direction of flow.

Horizontal Drain Transitions: Sanitary Tee vs. Wye

Choosing the correct fitting for horizontal drain transitions is critical to prevent flow obstruction and back-up issues. A standard sanitary tee is designed for transitioning flow from horizontal to vertical branches. Installing a sanitary tee flat on its side in a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage line creates turbulence and allows waste to flow backward or collect at the branch junction. Instead, always use a wye with a 1/8 bend or a combination wye and 1/8 bend for horizontal drainage direction changes to direct waste smoothly downstream in the direction of flow.
